analyst_view.overall: Early view: a game between two promoted sides near the bottom, with Coventry two points above the drop zone and Ipswich only two points better off. Coventry lost 3-1 at Everton without the injured Haji Wright, and Ipswich lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth with almost no open-play threat beyond Julio Enciso. Both defences leak goals, but nerves and two thin attacks argue for a tighter game than the numbers expect.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean a little lower: Coventry have scored only 10 in 10 games and are without Haji Wright (thigh), while Ipswich made just 0.30 expected goals from open play against Bournemouth. Both defences are poor (19 and 20 conceded), so goals will come, but 3.2 asks a lot of two blunt attacks in a nervy game.

corners.text: The site has 8.2 corners. I lean slightly higher because Ipswich play with wingers like Abdul Fatawu and Jaden Philogene, and Coventry play wide forwards such as Tatsuhiro Sakamoto and Yann Gboho. In a game where both sides need the points, I expect more pressure in wide areas than the figure suggests.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.0 cards. I lean higher: this is a relegation six-pointer between two sides in the bottom six, and Lampard was furious with the officials after the Everton game, which hints at a tense touchline. Low-card estimates usually hold for calm mid-table games, not this kind.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. I lean lower: Ipswich went most of the second half at Portman Road without a touch in the Bournemouth box, and Coventry lose a main striker in Wright. I still expect a fairly open game, but closer to the mid-20s.

shots_on_target.text: The site has 7.8 shots on target. I lean slightly lower because both attacks depend on one or two players (Enciso for Ipswich, Yann Gboho and Taiwo Awoniyi for Coventry) and neither creates many clear chances. Around seven feels right.
